claims.text: An Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni high-entropy alloy will have superior high-temperature tribo-corrosion resistance compared with conventional alloys.
The improved tribo-corrosion resistance results from stable protective oxide films formed during combined thermal, wear, and corrosion exposure.
The proposed material is a homogenized bulk Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni HEA made by conventional alloy processing.
The proposed exposure combines elevated temperature, cyclic mechanical wear, and a corrosive saline medium.
The relevant test-temperature range is approximately 400–600 °C.
Exposure will form a continuous and adherent oxide scale on the alloy surface.
The surface oxide scale will be enriched in Cr and Al.
The alloy's multiple principal elements promote rapid oxidation under high-temperature tribological stress.
The alloy's multiple principal elements promote formation of protective oxide layers under high-temperature tribological stress.
Oxide-mediated passivation minimizes metal dissolution.
Oxide-mediated passivation minimizes mechanical degradation.
Reduced metal dissolution and mechanical degradation slow overall tribo-corrosion.
The Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni HEA will exhibit a significantly lower wear rate than 316L stainless steel under identical conditions.
The Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni HEA will exhibit a significantly lower corrosion current density than 316L stainless steel under identical conditions.
The predicted reductions in wear rate and corrosion current density are caused by stabilization from protective oxide films.
Excessively high temperatures may compromise the protective oxide layer.
Extremely high mechanical loads may compromise the protective oxide layer.
Mechanical disruption beyond the oxide scale's self-healing capacity may compromise protection.
The magnitude of performance improvement may depend on processing conditions, exact alloy composition, and environmental conditions.

Failure to obtain statistically significant reductions in both wear rate and corrosion current density relative to 316L, or failure to observe a stable self-healing oxide scale, will falsify the hypothesis.
